Why add the std::move here?
Can it be a separate patch?

I was curious on why clang-tidy requested for this. On close inspection, what happened was I added `std::optional<sdbusplus::message::object_path> assertedLog;` to `struct Threshold` which made it no longer trivially copy-able. Hence the need for move. Its either that, or make the whichThreshold parameter pass-by-reference.
Resolving this if no concerns.

if i remember correctly, the generated code for xyz.openbmc_project.Logging.Entry
should define a constant for the interface name.
This is something which can really move towards using the new lg2::resolve() API.
Using the builtin resolve method in commit.hpp. Makes this a lot more cleaner.

Why define an inline lambda here?

Can this be a regular function?
Nothing preventing it. Let me move it out.
Moved it out to a function.
On second thoughts, I realized I could just use std::find_if instead of rolling my own.
That's a really long switch statement, can this be done using a map, or a separate function?
Yeah.... agreed. this is hard on the eyes. Let me move it into smallish helper functions.

Since these are almost identical except for the enum values and type, you might be able to make a template function for a lot of this.

```
assertThreshold<Level::SOFTSHUTDOWN, Errors::ReadingAboveUpperSoftShutdownThreshold, Errors::ReadingBelowLowerSoftShutdownThreshold>(direction, threhsold->assertedLog);
```

If you structure it right you might just be able to make N calls to this template and not worry about it being a switch-case statement.
Moved it to helper function. Im sure it can be prettier.
Thanks Patrick for the suggestion. Was able to make it much more easier to read using templates.
I believe I have addressed all the comments. I also ensured I re-run the tests to make sure I did not introduce any regressions since a good chunk of the code changed.
Others are valid nits, I will send updates.
whichThreshold was in sensor struct, right? Can it be safely moved here?
Thats pass by value. We are only moving the function parameter. which was copied.
ACK

Are we resolving an event log entry here?
Why?

I thought resolving event logs is a manual process.
https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/event-logging.md?plain=1#L236

> Applications running on the BMC should be able to determine when a previously
reported error is no longer relevant

Imagine a system repeatedly crossing critical thresholds on some sensor.
With this implementation, the EventLog entry is always set to resolved once the sensor value comes back to normal.

But the cause of the issue has not been determined, so it is not resolved?

Maybe i have some misunderstanding of how this is used in practice.

This patch is really doing 2 things at once:
- Adding structured logging for the Threshold Events
- Auto-resolving log entries

Maybe it would benefit the patch if it were split in 2 patches.

>> But the cause of the issue has not been determined, so it is not resolved?

I dont think thats the intention of the resolution for at least sensor threshold events. The issue was the sensor value was out-of-range. Once the sensor value is back in range, the issue is resolved. There may have been an underlying issue yes, the log entry is the proof of that.
nit: to be consistent with this package "\n";

nit: invert condition and return early to reduce the nesting
Acknowledged
why is this an error for "Unable to find threshold"?
Fair point. I added a new check with a new std::err which should prevent us from being confused.
nit: \n";
Acknowledged
It's unfortunate we even have this case as a possibility.  It means something is wrong with the configuration and we probably shouldn't even be running this sensor daemon.

My way of testing this was through externalsensor. My first attempt was copying https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/master/configurations/kudo_motherboard.json#L864 soon to realize the units needs to be xyz.openbmc_project.Sensor.Value.Unit.DegreesC and not DegreesC.

A possible path forward is to make sure the sensor->unit _is_ of type sdbusplus::common::xyz::openbmc_project::sensor::Value::Unit and the conversion from string is done at load.
Fixed it. Moved the conversion to the sensor initialization so we dont have to check every time.

Can I ask couple of questions regarding IPMI SEL?

1. How will these log messages be interperted in the `ipmitool sel log` output? Will they be mapped to the correct sensorIDs? (If this is the case, does it work only in dynamic IPMI compilation option, or is there any way to get it working with YAML approach? Does it work with the base code of ipmid, or is fb-ipmi-oem necessary to be present)

2. What will be with the systems that currently use sel-logger for threshold logging? Will they get duplicates for every threshold event SEL after this change?

(1) These are primarily for redfish side of things. Someone more familiar with IPMI SEL entries should update https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-host-ipmid/blob/master/selutility.cpp#L292.
 (2) Yes. If a platform is using phosphor-sel-logger with log-threshold option enabled, they will get duplicate logs. There are two options here:
   (a) Disable it (Now that I have put up https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-virtual-sensor/+/80773 (virtual sensors) and https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/pldm/+/77525 (pldm), it should not be needed anymore once all 3 gets merged (Some platforms might not use pldm or virtual sensors or both so it should not matter for those platforms)
   (b) Disable these, by adding filters: https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-logging?tab=readme-ov-file#event-log-filtering to phosphor-logging. I could propose these filters if it helps.

Hi @amithash@meta.com,
Currently, when dbus-sensors emits threshold event signal, the phosphor-sel-logger will create 2 journal logs for IPMI and Redfish.
If we disable log-threshold option in phosphor-sel-logger, no IPMI journal logs are created.
I think we have to add the code to add IPMI journal log in the Dbus-sensors also.

What is the "IPMI journal log"?  We shouldn't be adding IPMI-specific code in dbus-sensors.  If there is functionality missing, I suspect we need something in either:
- phosphor-logging (less likely)
- ipmi itself
- rsyslog magic

There is already an option in phosphor-logging to enable journal if that's something you want: https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-logging/blob/master/lib/lg2_commit.cpp#L132 .  This is the thing that might need some ipmi and/or rsyslog machinery to fully enable.

> Currently, when dbus-sensors emits threshold event signal, the phosphor-sel-logger will create 2 journal logs for IPMI and Redfish.

Using new-style events is an overall direction.  I'm fine if we point out what needs to be fixed and get it fixed, but we shouldn't hold up a dbus-sensors commit for a missing IPMI functionality.  We already have these events in other repositories.

I investigated the method applications are logging threshold events (dbus-sensors/phosphor-virtual-sensors/pldm. I see that they are emitting signals to phosphor-sel-logger to notify events. phosphor-sel-logger reads messages to create logs for both IPMI and Redfish.
I see that you are updating the method to log threshold events in dbus-sensors/phosphor-virtual-sensors/pldm, should we update phosphor-sel-logger instead?

> I see that you are updating the method to log threshold events in dbus-sensors/phosphor-virtual-sensors/pldm, should we update phosphor-sel-logger instead?

No.  phosphor-sel-logger is an optional component.  We should not rely on this for mainline behavior, such as reporting threshold events.

In my opinion, this was a poor implementation decision originally.
